raw_response:
I’ve farmed here a long time, so I won’t change too much unless there is a strong reason. On my 10.1 mu, I will keep most land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, about 6.5 mu, because that is the safest way to keep grain coming and spread the risk across two seasons. I’ll leave 3.6 mu in cotton for cash income. Cotton takes more hand work, but if the weather is decent it still helps the household have money in hand. With only two people at home, I have to be careful not to stretch labor too much, so I won’t expand cotton.

For wheat, I’ll sow in early to mid October on the same land where maize comes off. I usually use a common improved variety from the local dealer, not anything too fancy. I’ll put most fertilizer as base, then topdress once at jointing if the stand looks good. I know the extension people talk about more exact rates, but on my land I still trust what has worked: not too little, because wheat turns yellow fast if you hold back. I have well irrigation, but pumping costs money, so I’ll water mainly at the key times, not too many extra rounds.

For summer maize, the turnaround after wheat is very tight, so I’ll keep it simple and fast. After wheat harvest I’ll do quick residue handling and either light rotary tillage or direct seeding if I can get the machine in time. I use hybrid maize seed because the stand is better and yield is steadier. I’ll put part of the fertilizer near planting and part later around the big bell stage. If rain is decent, I may only irrigate once; if it stays dry, then twice. I don’t like to save too much on maize fertilizer because if maize falls behind in July, it’s hard to recover.

For cotton, I’ll keep a smaller area. Cotton brings cash, but it needs more watching for insects and more labor at picking. I’ll use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer, and then add some later if the plants are growing well. I won’t push cotton too hard because with my age and only two people in the house, too much cotton is tiring and risky. This year I’d rather keep a steady plan than gamble.
